narrative_prose:
"It's not just a storm," Hector yelled over the wind, adjusting his heavy harness. "It's a battery! A big, angry, floating battery!" He was strapped to the top of the Stormbreaker tower, fifty meters above the Enclave. Below him, emerald phase-space butterfly wings rotated gracefully across the brass-framed CRT monitors in the underground bunker, offering a quiet subterranean bioluminescent wonder against the harsh, chaotic ultraviolet auroras above.

"If you're complaining and no one is laughing, you're complaining wrong," Kaio's voice crackled through the comms. The scout was breathless, scrambling up the exterior rungs to join him on the perilous platform.

"I'm not complaining, I'm narrating," Hector grinned, watching the bruised, violent purple clouds. "We are utilizing real-time Lorenz strange-attractor bifurcation targeting that fires millisecond pre-strike ionization pulses to lock chaotic lightning onto collector rods at 98% efficiency. We attract the strike, consume the gigajoules into the bedrock geode, and defend the Enclave from the shear wave. The storm doesn't stand a chance."

"Targeting solution is locked," Jane droned boredly in his earpiece. "Firing the femtosecond laser... now."

A violet beam pierced the cloud layer, ionizing a conductive path of plasma. A blinding pillar of white fire slammed down the channel, the tower vibrating with impossible kinetic force. Hector's heart hammered in perfect sync with the thunder. He reached for the heavy, pulsing copper baton—the physical telemetry drive that needed to be rushed to the lower relay—when he froze.

His Virgo override kicked in, cold and terrifying. The thrill vanished, replaced by an obsessive, paralyzing fixation on the heavy coupling attached to the baton's housing. It was misaligned. Half a degree off vertical.

"The coupling," Hector muttered, his adrenaline suddenly failing him. "The coupling is 0.5 degrees asymmetrical. The inductance will wobble. We have to conceal the core readings until it's perfect. The atmospheric pressure is dropping fourteen hectopascals a second, it's going to breach!"

"Hector? What are you doing?" Kaio hauled himself over the final rung, rain slicking his carapace-armor. "Pass the baton!"

"I can't! If I hand it off, the asymmetry will corrupt the 5D quartz storage! I have to realign it," Hector shouted, fumbling frantically with his heavy gloves to adjust the massive brass nut.

Kaio didn't argue. He recognized the friction of the moment. He reached out, his own hands steady as he braced against the gale. "I've got the lower half. Turn on three. One. Two. Three!"

With a shared grunt, they torqued the coupling the necessary half-degree. The harmonic hum of the baton smoothed out instantly. Hector let out a breath he didn't know he was holding, the crippling perfectionism breaking as quickly as it had arrived. He unclipped the telemetry drive and shoved it securely against Kaio's chest.

"Go!" Hector yelled, clapping the scout on the shoulder. "Don't drop it, or Jane will make us dig the grounding trenches by hand!"

Kaio flashed a wild grin, securing the baton and turning to rappel down the spire into the safety of the bunker.
summary: Hector utilizes femtosecond lasers to harness gigajoule planetary lightning strikes, but becomes paralyzed by a 0.5-degree cable misalignment due to his Virgo override, requiring Kaio's help to realign it and complete the physical baton handoff.
